obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise
citation: Merchant agreement covering all 10 MIDs (fictional contract term); N72-R01
trigger: Suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to card data or a payment system, including an acquirer common-point-of-purchase alert
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (contract term; fictional)
notify: Acquiring bank risk line by phone, then in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
clock_starts: Time of suspicion recorded in the incident log

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, version 10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (North America contact in Table 1.1), normally coordinated through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - card brand rule applied through the merchant agreement

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2 and Attachment A
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Security Manager and Chief Financial Officer

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days
notify: Visa, through the acquirer's upload tools
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Discovery of at-risk accounts or the window of exposure

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the acquirer; the PFI must not have provided other services to the company, so the QSA firm that supports the SAQ D is not used as PFI
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required by Visa (Visa may instead require an independent investigation, Section A.6)
owner: Chief Financial Officer with the General Counsel

obligation: Other card brands (Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per the brand's rules; timing not verified here. Follow the acquirer's instructions and treat 24 hours as the working target
notify: Brand, normally through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm with the acquirer

citation: Franchise agreements for Hotels 3 to 6 (fictional contract term)
trigger: Suspected compromise of brand systems (SYS-02, brand terminals, brand firewalls) or of guest data at a franchised hotel
deadline: Within 24 hours (contract term; fictional)
notify: Franchisor's incident contact, by phone and in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when Hotels 3 to 6, brand systems, or brand guest data may be affected

obligation: Hotel owner notice under the REIT management agreement
citation: Hotel management agreement with the lodging REIT (fictional contract term), from 2027-01-01
trigger: Suspected security incident affecting the managed hotels' data or systems
deadline: Within 48 hours (contract term; fictional)
notify: The REIT's asset management and legal contacts named in the agreement
applies_at_this_tier: From 2027-01-01 only

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the hotel owner (outbound)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains as third-party agent for the REIT-owned hotels' guest data
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after determining the breach or reason to believe it occurred. The company must give the owner all information it needs for its own notices
notify: The REIT (covered entity), which gives the 501.171(3) and (4) notices; the company may give them on the owner's behalf under 501.171(6)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: From 2027-01-01 only; the 48-hour contract term is shorter and controls in practice
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the company (SYS-01 vendor, chatbot, contact center, CRM, payroll, staffing companies) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The company (Security Manager and General Counsel); the company then gives the 501.171(3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in contracts (STD-03 asks Tier 1 vendors for 72 hours)

trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information of Florida residents. Includes a name with a driver license, ID card, or passport number (ID scans), with a card number in combination with any required security code (CRO keyed payments, card forms, recordings), or with biometric data (time clock templates)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 additional days are available only for this notice, if good cause is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email; substitute notice (website plus print and broadcast media) only if cost exceeds $250,000, more than 500,000 people are affected, or contact details are missing (501.171(4)(f))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination. No extension applies to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with a synopsis, the number of Florida individuals, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if this path is used; counsel decides. Unlikely for card data with security codes

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing; it may extend or revoke the delay in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request in the decision log
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: Affected guests and employees who reside outside Florida (most resort guests live in other states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3.3.4 (recommended); OFAC advisory (mitigating factor)
trigger: Suspected card compromise or ransomware
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office (named in the Visa document); FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if extortion occurs. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

citation: Cyber insurance policy ($10 million limit, $250,000 retention; contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging counsel, forensics, or any other incident vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

trigger: Severity 1 incident (card compromise, ransomware, or confirmed data theft)
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration
notify: Audit committee chair; the private equity sponsor's board representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would likely be covered because it exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 721110 (proposed 226.2(a)); lodging has no sector criterion. Voluntary reporting to CISA is encouraged now
clock_starts: Proposed: reasonable belief that a covered incident occurred

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held and files no SEC reports

trigger: Breach of unsecured protected health information
deadline: Within 60 days of discovery (individuals)
notify: Individuals, HHS, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a covered entity or business associate (the spas provide no medical services)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
